prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Render one high-fidelity desktop web application screen for CommandGrid, a hackathon infrastructure recovery simulator. Landscape 16:10 edge to edge, crisp readable text. No browser window, no device or desk. This is a static mockup using fictional sample data, not a landing page.
Direction B — civic systems. An operator needs to understand degraded systems and execute recovery actions. Make a bright, exceptionally designed working interface inspired by Swiss public-information design, transport wayfinding and Awwwards' confident typography. Use a cool white ground, deep cobalt as a decisive structural color, dark navy type, amber warnings, and pale mint status. Humanist sans-serif headings and tabular numbers. Strong alignment, generous breathing room, deliberate asymmetry, clean flat controls and divided rows rather than boxes inside boxes. Let a cobalt system-health overview lead, balanced by an incident/action workspace; this is not a conventional four-card dashboard.
Frame: simple text CommandGrid, slim left navigation Dashboard / Mission Builder / Objectives / Mission Control / Reports with Mission Control active; utility line “Sample scenario”. Heading “Communications Recovery”, Running, “03:42 / 10:00”, “Pause”. Metrics: Communications 82%, Equipment 75%, Power 64%, Resources 58%. Content: a precise connected-node diagram for North Haven Relay, Cedar Support Center, Juniper Power Station; the power station is degraded. Incident “Power failure”, recovery choice “Activate backup power”, cost “8 resources”, button “Execute action”. A visible timeline of recent recovery events and a restrained telemetry trend. Smaller objective status “Restore power”.
Prioritize clear hierarchy and large enough text to actually read. Give the screen one dominant compositional idea with supporting data quieter. No testimonials, invented financial claims, success probabilities, decorative 3D objects, excessive rounding, icon tiles, gradients or poster-style slogans. A finished usable app interface with the craftsmanship of an independent design studio.
